header.business: A US criminal and traffic defense law firm
header.mode: next quarter's budget, plus the channel to test next
header.total_set_by: the last 90 days' spend as a monthly run-rate (decision plus trend window ÷ 3), as asked
header.result_counted: Google Ads conversions (calls and form leads), every lead counted the same: no value per result was given
header.yardstick_set_by: blended cost per result of all non-brand lines over the decision window (no target given)
header.limits: none given; brand search left alone; 10% test reserve (next-quarter mode default)
header.platforms_read: Google Ads (1 account). No other ad platform and no GA4 property is connected for this business.

headline: Criminal Defense is the cheapest place for the next lead: $21 on Google's own simulation against a $32 yardstick. Grow it from $1,060 to $1,800 a month in three weekly steps.

Drug Charges, Nursing Board and DUI give back $690 a month from Oct 20, once the Oct 1 budget edits have settled. Confirm what a drug or license case is worth first: at the same value per lead they cost 4 to 5 times the yardstick.
Set aside $570 a month for a Microsoft Ads test, starting December 1 once the rollout's last step (Nov 3) is done. All of today's spend sits on one platform.

current_state.not_read: Meta, Microsoft Ads, LinkedIn, TikTok, Pinterest, Snapchat, X and OpenAI Ads: not connected for this business. GA4: not connected for this business.
current_state.budget_edits_found: 24 budget edits and 3 bid-target edits in the last 14 days, most of them on Oct 1. Judged by net change per campaign: today's daily budgets add up to $265, against $385 14 days ago.
current_state.current_level_rule: current level = the lower of 30-day spend and today's daily budget x 30.4, because Google never charges more than that in a month

reasons: Criminal Defense: +$740 a month. Star at $19 a lead (0.59 x T), improving, loses 42% of impressions to budget, and Google's simulation puts the next lead at $21.
Drug Charges: -$310 a month. Bleeder at $166 a lead (5.15 x T) on 5 results. Starts after 2026-10-15, when the Oct 1 budget change has settled.

DUI: -$190 a month. Underperformer at $48 a lead (1.48 x T) on 16 results, worsening; 54% of impressions lost to rank, which more budget would not fix. Starts after 2026-10-15, when the Oct 1 budget change has settled.
Nursing Board: -$190 a month. Bleeder at $131 a lead (4.07 x T) on 3 results. Starts after 2026-10-15, when the Oct 1 budget change has settled.

Traffic Tickets: held at its new $35 daily budget ($1,060 a month). A Star at $24 a lead losing 27% to budget, but its estimated next lead ($26) costs more than Criminal Defense's simulated one, so it is next in line when the total grows.
Brand, Out-of-State Traffic (Borderline, worsening), Out-of-State DUI and Pharmacy Board (too little data): unchanged.
recommended_split.cost_of_limits: none: brand search is the only limit, and it has no headroom to fund (90% impression share) and no reason to cut
recommended_split.concentration: Google Ads holds 100% of the plan, which is a dependency risk, not an error. The test reserve is the plan's answer to it.

scenarios.risk: lowest: no cuts are needed because the run-rate gap covers the funding cap
moderate: cuts wait for settling, funding goes to the one line with a simulation
highest: Drug Charges and Nursing Board switched off before their lead value is known

scenarios.scenario: naive reference (budget in proportion to 1 ÷ cost per result; ignores saturation, never the recommendation)
scenarios.note: would put 31% of the budget on brand search, which is already at 90% impression share

assumptions: Gains use the line's marginal cost per result; losses use the line's own cost per result, which overstates the loss a little because a line's last dollars buy the least.

Changes are measured against each line's actual 30-day spend. Traffic Tickets loses results, and Drug Charges loses more than its plan cut, because their Oct 1 budget cuts already cap them below what they spent in the window.
Results from the test reserve are counted as zero until the test has data.
Google's budget simulations are Google's own models of the last 7 days; the headroom multipliers are rules of thumb. Both are estimates.
confidence_why: the only funded line's next-dollar cost comes from Google's own budget simulation
two of the cut lines are judged on spend with under 10 results each (Drug Charges and Nursing Board)
results come from one platform, so no cross-platform claim check is needed; no GA4 property is connected for this business either
no value per result was given, so every lead counts the same

seasonality.flag: last year's 2025-11 clicks were 34% below the July-September average; held at 1.00 until you confirm it was demand, not a pause or budget cut

next_quarter_by_month.seasonality_source: last year's monthly clicks (2025-07-01 to 2025-12-31), indexed to the July-September average

months.test_reserve_note: the test reserve starts Dec 1, the first full month after the rollout's last step (Nov 3); until then it stays unspent

months.gate: last rollout step on Nov 3; then release only if Criminal Defense kept its cost per result within 1.25 x the marginal cost used ($26) over the previous 4 weeks
months.test_reserve_note: the test reserve starts Dec 1, the first full month after the rollout's last step (Nov 3); until then it stays unspent

months.gate: release only if Criminal Defense kept its cost per result within 1.25 x the marginal cost used ($26) over the previous 4 weeks

if_the_total_can_grow.stops_because: Traffic Tickets' headroom has dropped to low after its funding steps; Criminal Defense has doubled (the +100% cap). No other line is a judged Star or Solid, so nothing else qualifies.

channel_mix.why: Google Search works for this business and the buyer searches at the moment of need (a ticket, an arrest, a board letter). Microsoft Ads sells the same intent on another network, and the Google campaigns can be imported to start.
not_now: Meta and TikTok: urgent legal needs start with a search, not a feed. No data here to test against.
LinkedIn: could reach nurses and pharmacists by job title for board defense, but Nursing Board already costs 4 x T on search. Revisit only if a license case is worth several times a ticket case.

test_budget.timing: The reserve starts Dec 1, so $560 by Dec 31 buys about 12 results at 1.5 x T. At $570 a month the 30th result lands around Feb 17, 2027, when the continue-or-kill decision is made. A reserve of $1,450 in December would decide it by Dec 31.
test_budget.continue_when: cost per result at or under $40 (1.25 x T) after 30 results
test_budget.kill_when: $970 spent (3 x T x 10) with fewer than 10 results, or over $64 (2 x T) after 30 results
test_budget.status: untested: no Microsoft Ads account is connected for this business

rollout.rule: a daily budget moves at most 25% of today's budget per weekly step; the target is the new monthly level ÷ 30.4; settling lines start after their settle date
rollout.check_before_each_step: Criminal Defense kept its cost per result within $26 (1.25 x the marginal cost used), and the cut lines didn't lose more leads than projected

changes_offered.note: not run: offered only after the user says yes. The budget is not shared, so only this campaign changes.

monitoring: Weekly: each line's cost per result against its projection, spend against budget, and any limit being hit.
Daily in the first week after each rollout step: spend against the new daily budget, so a step that under- or over-delivers is caught early.
rebalancing_triggers: A line's cost per result runs 20% over its projection for 2 weeks in a row.
A line spends less than 85% of its budget for 2 weeks in a row.
A new offer, a season change, a tracking change, or another round of budget edits like Oct 1.

risks.risk: Criminal Defense gets more expensive faster than the simulation says
risks.shows_as: cost per result above $26 after a step
risks.do: stop at the current step and send the next step to Traffic Tickets

risks.risk: The cut lines carry higher-value cases
risks.shows_as: the firm values a drug or license case at 4 to 5 times a ticket case
risks.do: rerun with a value per result before Oct 20; the cuts may disappear

risks.shows_as: November clicks fall about a third
risks.do: the month's gate catches it; unspent money stays unspent rather than moving to weaker lines

risks.shows_as: any Google policy, auction or tracking change hits 100% of leads
risks.do: run the Microsoft Ads test from December 1
